battle.name: 秦滅齊之戰
battle.brief: 公元前221年（秦王政二十六年），秦將王翦率眾自燕地南下，進逼齊都臨淄。齊相後勝私通秦國、主降，客卿淳于髡勸王拒秦不從，齊王建遂不戰而降，受封平原君，齊地改置郡縣，秦統一六國。卡面埃及長矛屬青銅早王朝工藝，與本役相隔約三千年，不在戰場上；同期秦軍用鐵矛、秦弩，齊軍倚重車騎與弓弩。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 秦滅齊之戰是公元前221年秦王政二十六年，秦對東方最後一個諸侯國齊國的滅國之戰，也是秦統一六國戰爭的收官一役。交戰一方是秦：以關中、蜀郡、巴郡的耕戰體制為經濟基礎，國家機器高度組織，兵源、糧秣、鐵料與銅器來源皆有制度化的供應，軍隊編制以步兵方陣為主，輔以車兵、騎兵、弩兵與攻城部隊，最高統帥是秦王政本人，滅韓、趙、魏、楚、燕皆出自王翦、王賁、李信等將領之手，滅齊一役《史記·齊太公世家》記為「秦將王翦將二十萬眾伐齊」。另一方是齊：姜姓傳至田氏，累封於海岱之間，都臨淄，國富兵強曾為東方首國，齊之車騎、冶鐵與煮鹽並稱於天下；然自前284年燕軍樂毅破齊，至前279年田單收復失地，國力大損，此後二十餘年國勢陵夷，朝廷分為主戰與主降兩派。齊國並非以全軍力應戰，而是在秦軍壓境、內外交困之下，由齊王建代表政府接受秦的條件；齊國主力兵團未成建制集結即告解體，故本役的交戰方，實為一場實力懸殊的收編，而不是兩軍對攻的正面會戰。
countriesEn: The Qin conquest of Qi was the war in which, in the twenty-sixth year of the reign of King Zheng of Qin (221 BC), the state of Qin destroyed Qi, the last of the eastern vassal states, and it was also the closing campaign of the wars that unified the Six States. One belligerent was Qin: an economy built on the farming-and-war system of Guanzhong, Shu and Ba, a highly organised state machine, and institutionalised supplies of manpower, grain, iron and copper; its army was organised around infantry formations supported by chariotry, cavalry, crossbowmen and siege specialists, with King Zheng himself as supreme commander, and the destruction of Han, Zhao, Wei, Chu and Yan had been carried out by generals such as Wang Jian, Wang Ben and Li Xin. The Records of the Historian, in the House of Tian, states of the Qi campaign: the Qin general Wang Jian led two hundred thousand men to attack Qi. The other belligerent was Qi: the Jiang lineage had passed to the Tian house, enfeoffed across the lands between the sea and Mount Tai, with its capital at Linzi, once the richest and strongest of the eastern states, its chariots and cavalry, its ironworking and its salt-boiling famous throughout the realm. Yet from the breach of Qi by the Yan general Yue Yi in 284 BC to the recovery of the lost ground by Tian Dan in 279 BC, the country was badly drained, and over the following twenty-odd years its fortunes declined steadily while the court split into a party for war and a party for surrender. Qi did not meet the full weight of its army: under military pressure on one side and internal collapse on the other, the government represented by King Jian of Qi accepted Qin's terms. Qi's main body of troops never assembled as a coherent force before it dissolved, so what took place was in truth the annexation of a vastly outmatched opponent, not a set-piece battle between two armies.
people: 此役的關鍵人物分屬兩營。秦方：秦王政在位三十七年，自前230年滅韓起，前228年滅趙，前225年滅魏，前223年滅楚，前226年王翦破燕，前222年王賁追擒燕王喜於遼東，至前221年已把六國之中五國掃清，滅齊遂成定局；大將王翦是《史記》明載的統兵者，滅楚用六十萬大軍、歷年而拔郢，滅燕又統二十萬眾，《史記·齊太公世家》記他將二十萬眾伐齊、拔臨淄、虜齊王建，然《史記·白起王翦列傳》載王翦卒於前222年，兩說先後抵觸，是本役記載上最明顯的史料矛盾之一，一般以為《齊太公世家》誤繫名將，或其實由王賁等人統兵而托名王翦。尉繚在《史記·尉繚列傳》獻策，主張對齊先絕其外援、離間其君臣，與本役不戰而定的走向相合；廷尉李斯則以治獄與書同文、郡縣改制一類文書工作支應統一。齊方：齊王建在位數十年，目睹國勢陵夷而無力振作，終以朝議決策、遣使請降，被秦封為平原君、徙於薛，日後客死異鄉；齊相後勝受秦之賄，倡議不戰，歷來史家以此為齊亡之咎；前284年破齊的燕將樂毅、前279年以火牛陣復國的田單，是齊國盛衰的兩個轉折人物，而稷下學宮與一批辯士，則是齊國在制度與思想上最後的存量。
peopleEn: The decisive personalities of this campaign fall into two camps. On the Qin side, King Zheng of Qin had reigned thirty-seven years; since the destruction of Han in 230 BC he had taken Zhao in 228, Wei in 225 and Chu in 223, and Wang Jian had broken Yan in 226 while Wang Ben pursued Yan king Xi and took him prisoner in Liaodong in 222, so by 221 BC five of the six states were already swept away and the destruction of Qi had become a settled plan. The general Wang Jian is the commander named in the historical record: he took Chu with six hundred thousand men, taking years to reach Ying, and again led two hundred thousand against Yan; the House of Tian in the Records of the Historian records that he led two hundred thousand men against Qi, took Linzi and captured King Jian of Qi. Yet the Biography of Bai Qi and Wang Jian in the same work states that Wang Jian died in 222 BC. The two statements collide in sequence, and this is the most obvious documentary contradiction attaching to this campaign; the usual view is that the House of Tian attached the wrong general's name, or that the force was really led by Wang Ben or another commander and credited to Wang Jian. Wei Liao, in the Biography of Wei Liao, advised cutting off Qi's outside support and sowing dissension among its ruler and ministers, which fits the course of a campaign settled without a battle; the judicial official Li Si supported the unification through documentary and legal work such as the standardisation of writing and the establishment of commanderies and counties. On the Qi side, King Jian of Qi reigned for several decades, watched the state decline and lacked the strength to reverse it, and in the end took a decision in council and sent envoys to surrender; Qin made him Lord of Pingyuan and moved him to Xue, where he would die in exile. The Qi chancellor Hou Sheng took bribes from Qin and advocated giving up the fight, and historians have long blamed him for the fall of Qi. Yue Yi, the Yan general who broke Qi in 284 BC, and Tian Dan, who recovered the country with a fire-oxen formation in 279 BC, were the two turning-point figures in Qi's rise and decline, while the Jixia academy and its school of speakers represented the last residue of Qi in matters of institutions and thought.
kits: 卡面的埃及長矛是早王朝時期的工藝：銅或青銅矛頭以綁扎方式固定在木杆上，形制簡素，主要用於守城垣與收復失地。它在本卡的位置是長兵器技術譜系的起點，而不是本役的實戰裝備——以公元前3200年計，它比秦滅齊早出約二千八百年，出土於埃及與兩河流域的這類矛，與臨淄城下秦軍所用的鐵矛並不屬於同一技術世代。本役現場的秦軍武備以鐵為主：長兵器有鐵矛、戈、戟，戈援細長而內柲，適合勾啄與橫擊；短兵有秦劍，身長約六十至七十厘米，格部常飾同心圓紋，出土劍具多硬直而兼顧刺與劈；投射武器有弓與弩，秦弩屬張弦式，弩臂長約一米四，需以腰足之力上弦，另有可連發的機弩，箭鏃多見三棱形與雙翼形，側面可減空氣阻力。防護為皮甲、札甲與漆盾，車兵用戎車，一乘載御者、射手與持戈卒三人。攻城器械包括雲梯、飛石機、巢車與臨衝車，可見此役的攻城技術已相當成熟，惜未有用武之地。齊軍則以車騎見長，齊車兵在列國之中最為精銳，兼有齊長城沿泰山、沂水一線布防的工事體系；齊地山東出鐵，冶鐵與煮鹽同為其立國之本的產業。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card is Early Dynastic workmanship: a copper or bronze head fixed to a wooden shaft by binding, a plain form used chiefly for holding city walls and for recovering lost ground. Its place on this card is as the starting point of the technical lineage of pole weapons, not as the service equipment of this campaign. Dated to about 3200 BC, it precedes the conquest of Qi by some twenty-eight centuries, and such spears recovered from Egypt and Mesopotamia do not belong to the same technological generation as the iron spears the Qin soldiers carried before Linzi. The Qin armament actually present in this campaign was predominantly iron. Pole weapons included iron spears, ge and ji, the long curved blade of the ge with its inner tang suited to hooking and to lateral blows; close weapons included the Qin sword, sixty to seventy centimetres long, its guard often decorated with concentric rings, the excavated blades stiff and serving both the thrust and the cut. Missiles included the bow and the crossbow; the Qin crossbow was of the tension-cocked type, with an arm about 1.4 metres long that had to be drawn by the strength of the waist and the leg, and there were repeating crossbows as well, with arrowheads commonly in three-edged and double-winged forms whose lateral facets reduce air resistance. Protection consisted of hide armour, lamellar armour and lacquered shields, while chariotry used the war chariot carrying three men: a driver, an archer and a halberdier. Siege equipment included scaling ladders, stone-throwers, tower carts and battering rams, showing that siegecraft in this campaign was already highly developed, though it had no occasion to be used. Qi's strength lay in chariots and cavalry, its chariot troops being among the finest in the world of the states, backed by the Qi Great Wall built along the line of Mount Tai and the Yi River; iron was produced in eastern Qi, where ironworking and salt-boiling together formed the economic base of the state.
tactics: 秦滅齊的戰術，屬於統一戰爭的最後一步，核心不在攻城而在斷援與屈兵。整體序列是「遠交近攻」：先與遠方國家往來以孤立近鄰，再以次數有限的會戰逐一消滅。滅齊前的十年間，秦沒有對齊用兵，反而在齊的西面先取韓、趙、魏，又於前284年後趁燕攻齊之際把燕拉到自己一側，使齊的西、南兩翼相繼崩解，最後才自燕地南下，以一支前出之軍直趨濟水北岸，兵鋒不取聊城、莒、即墨等齊國西部要地，唯以大軍壓向臨淄。配合此一軍事施壓，秦在齊的朝廷內部著手：以財貨結其主降之臣，使齊廷自喪鬥志；主戰一派曾謀據莒、即墨固守，《史記·滑稽列傳》記客卿淳于髡以狡兔三穴之喻進說，齊王不聽，而秦軍抵近之日，齊國並未組織有效的守城部署，臨淄城守與齊長城防線都未真正派上用場。降後秦軍入臨淄，收繳齊廷武備與府庫，齊王建受封平原君，收其地為齊郡、琅邪郡編戶，其兵器甲士分別納入秦國郡縣兵制與工官體系；秦統一後更令收天下兵器、聚之咸陽，銷為鐘鐻，整場戰爭以一次成功的政治兼併收尾。
tacticsEn: The tactics Qin employed against Qi belong to the final step of the unification wars, and their core lay not in storming walls but in cutting off aid and bending the enemy. The overall sequence was that of befriending the distant and attacking the near: opening relations with far-off states in order to isolate immediate neighbours, and then destroying them one by one in a limited number of set-piece engagements. In the ten years before the fall of Qi, Qin did not fight Qi directly. It instead took Han, Zhao and Wei on Qi's western side, and after 284 BC, when Yan moved against Qi, drew Yan over to its own side, so that Qi's western and southern flanks collapsed in turn. Only then did it send a forward force south out of Yan territory, driving straight for the north bank of the Ji River, declining to take the western strongpoints of Qiu, Ju and Jimo and pressing on Linzi with the mass of the army instead. Alongside this military pressure Qin worked inside the Qi court: buying off the ministers who favoured surrender so that the court lost its own will to fight. The party for war had proposed falling back on Ju and Jimo to hold out, and the Shiji's Biography of the Humorous enters the minister Chunyu Kun counselling the king with the image of the burrow with three entrances, but the king would not listen; by the time the Qin army drew near, Qi had organised no effective defence, and neither the garrison of Linzi nor the Qi Great Wall was ever put to serious use. After the surrender the Qin army entered Linzi and took over the weapons stores and treasury of the court; King Jian of Qi was made Lord of Pingyuan, his territory enrolled as the commanderies of Qi and Langya, and his weapons and soldiers were folded into the Qin county system and its workshops. After unification Qin further ordered that the weapons of all the realm be gathered at Xianyang and melted down into bells and weights, and the whole campaign closed as a successful political annexation.
data: 可確定的數字有限，須分辨史料層次。兵力：秦軍伐齊之數，《史記·齊太公世家》作「王翦將二十萬眾伐齊」，此為同時代記載中最常被引用的數字；惟秦軍歷次大役皆在二十萬至六十萬之間，反映的是大軍團作戰的常態規模，而非精確點算。齊方：戰國策士為游說而作的夸張之辭如「地方千里，帶甲百萬」，不宜作實數看待；但可確知者為齊國疆域之大、鹽鐵之利之厚、臨淄之盛，《史記·齊太公世家》稱其都臨淄「車轂擊，人肩摩，連袂成帷，舉袂成幕」，考古所見齊臨淄故城大城周長約二十公里，是同時代東亞最大城邑之一。距離與行程：秦軍自燕地南下，跨越濟水，進至臨淄城下，屬數百里之內的近距離會師，與滅楚時自漢中東出的長途征伐完全不同。時間：自前230年滅韓至前221年滅齊，秦的統一戰爭歷時約十年，而滅齊一役本身在秦王政二十六年內迅速完成，兵不血刃。編制：秦統一後分天下為三十六郡（後增至四十餘郡），齊地析置齊郡、琅邪郡，文字、度量衡、貨幣（半兩）、車軌一統，並收天下兵器聚之咸陽，銷為鐘鐻。
dataEn: The numbers that can be fixed are few, and the layers of the sources must be separated. On the numbers of men: the Records of the Historian in the House of Tian gives the Qi campaign as Wang Jian leading two hundred thousand men, and this is the figure most often quoted from contemporary accounts. But since the Qin armies in every great campaign ranged between two hundred thousand and six hundred thousand, the figure reflects the normal scale of a mass army in operation rather than an exact head count. On the Qi side: the inflated figures of the Warring States persuaders, such as a thousand li of territory and a million men under arms, cannot be treated as real numbers. What can be confirmed is the size of Qi's territory, the thickness of its salt and iron revenues and the wealth of Linzi; the House of Tian in the Records of the Historian describes its capital Linzi as one where the hubs of carts strike one another and the shoulders of men brush, with robes drawn together into a curtain and sleeves lifted into a canopy. Archaeologically, the great city of the Qi Linzi site has a circuit of roughly twenty kilometres and is among the largest urban settlements of eastern Asia in its age. On distance and route: the Qin army came south from Yan, crossed the Ji River and advanced to the walls of Linzi, a meeting engagement within a few hundred li, entirely unlike the long march east out of Hanzhong in the war against Chu. On time: from the destruction of Han in 230 BC to the destruction of Qi in 221 BC, Qin's unification wars ran for roughly a decade, while the Qi campaign itself was completed swiftly within the twenty-sixth year of King Zheng, with not a single arrow fired. On structure: after unification Qin divided the realm into thirty-six commanderies, later increased to more than forty; in Qi's land it established the commanderies of Qi and Langya, unified the script, the measures and weights, the coinage in half-liang pieces and the axle widths, and gathered the weapons of all the realm at Xianyang to be melted into bells and weights.
cause: 秦滅齊有遠近兩層原因。遠因是秦本身的制度優勢：商鞅變法之後的耕戰國家，郡縣編戶、軍功爵制與兵器官營，使秦能以一國之力逐個吃掉對手，而不必像早期分封諸侯那樣受限於血緣與地緣；秦王政又用「遠交近攻」的外交次序，把東方諸國彼此隔絕，最後留下國力最雄、位置最東的齊國作為唯一對手。齊自身的崩壞是近因：前284年燕將樂毅乘五國伐齊之勢入臨淄，取城七十餘座，前279年田單雖以火牛陣收復故土，國勢已非舊觀；此後湣王、襄王與王建三朝，齊廷並非沒有警覺，稷下學宮與一批辯士尚在，但因齊國富庶而四鄰皆欲分之，國君的作為屢被史家指為不理國事、好田獵，救亡之論屢見而不行，遂致邊患日迫、內廷渙散。秦滅燕之後，齊失去北面的屏障，濟水一線再無緩衝，滅齊遂成秦統一的最後一步；史家又謂秦在齊廷內部收買主降之臣，內外並進，使齊國在兵臨城下之前便已喪失戰意。
causeEn: The destruction of Qi by Qin had causes at two removes. The distant cause was Qin's own institutional superiority: as a farming-and-war state built after Shang Yang's reforms, with counties and registered households, ranks awarded for military merit and state monopolies over the arming of troops, Qin was able to take its opponents one at a time with the resources of a single country, without being constrained as the early enfeoffed lords were by blood ties and geography. King Zheng further used a diplomatic order of befriending the distant and attacking the near, which set the eastern states mutually isolated, leaving Qi, the most powerful and the most easterly of them, as the sole remaining opponent. The collapse of Qi itself was the proximate cause. In 284 BC the Yan general Yue Yi took advantage of the coalition of five states against Qin to enter Linzi and take more than seventy cities; in 279 BC Tian Dan recovered the old country with a formation of fire oxen, yet the state was never the same again. Through the reigns of King Min, King Xiang and King Jian, the Qi court was not without warning signs: the Jixia academy and a body of skilled speakers were still there. But because Qi was rich and its neighbours all coveted it, the conduct of its rulers was repeatedly faulted by historians for attending to hunting and neglect of state, proposals for salvation were repeatedly advanced and never carried out, and the pressure from the frontier grew while the court dissolved. Once Qin had destroyed Yan, Qi lost the screen to its north and the line of the Ji River left no buffer, so the destruction of Qi became the last step of Qin's unification. Historians add that Qin bought over the ministers who favoured surrender within the Qi court, attacking from within and without, so that Qi had already lost the will to fight before the enemy stood at its gates.
impact: 秦滅齊不只結束一場戰爭，也終結了一種政治與文化形態。政治上，齊是西周封建體系在東方的最後一個大型封國，自姜太公受封訖至前221年，延續約八百餘年；秦以郡縣制取代分封，齊王建封為平原君而實為俘囚，齊國宗廟社稷至此斷絕，其地編入帝國版圖，成為秦漢以後齊魯的行政與地理單位。思想上，齊自桓公、管仲以來便是東方文化的重鎮，稷下學宮盛時，百家爭鳴的諸子多出齊地，荀子講學稷下，淳于髡、鄒衍一類學者皆以齊為舞台；秦統一天下後行書同文、銷兵器、罷百家而尊術士，齊地學脈在焚書與避亂中斷裂，其緒餘直至漢初齊魯經學整理六藝時才重新接續。經濟上，齊的鐵冶、煮鹽、陶業與臨淄的手工業為秦朝提供了最厚的一層財政底子，秦遷六國豪族富室於咸陽，齊人亦隨軍師、隨徵役而西徙與南遷，齊文化的痕跡隨之散入關中、中原與荊楚。歷史的反面則是齊地的反秦：前208年陳涉部將武臣、曹參等入趙，田榮、昭陽朝先後據齊，項梁起兵於齊地薛，項羽以楚人而隨軍滅秦，滅國之恨與士族記憶，成為秦朝速亡的助力。
impactEn: The destruction of Qi by Qin ended not merely a war but a whole political and cultural order. Politically, Qi was the last great fief of the Western Zhou feudal system in the east, lasting for more than eight hundred years from the enfeoffment of Jiang Taigong down to 221 BC. Qin replaced enfeoffment with the commandery-and-county system, made King Jian of Qi a Lord of Pingyuan who was in effect a captive, and Qi's ancestral temple and altars came to an end there; its territory was folded into the empire and became the administrative and geographical unit of Qilu in later Qin and Han times. Intellectually, Qi had been the great centre of eastern culture since Duke Huan and Guan Zhong, and in the heyday of the Jixia academy most of the contending masters of the Hundred Schools came from Qi, with Xunzi lecturing at Jixia and scholars such as Chunyu Kun and Zou Yan taking Qi as their stage. After Qin unified the realm it enforced a single script, gathered in the weapons, and dismissed the Hundred Schools in favour of the court diviners; the Qi scholarly line was broken by the burning of books and by flight, and its surviving threads were not picked up again until the Qi-Lu classical learning of the early Han set the Six Arts in order. Economically, Qi's ironworking, salt-boiling, pottery and the workshops of Linzi supplied the Qin dynasty with the thickest layer of its fiscal base; Qin moved the wealthy and powerful families of the six states to Xianyang, and Qi people were moved west and south as soldiers and as labourers, scattering the marks of Qi culture into Guanzhong, the Central Plain and Jingchu. The reverse side of the story is the anti-Qin resistance of the Qi region: in 208 BC Wu Chen, Cao Shen and others of Chen Sheng's army entered Zhao, Tian Rong and Zhaoyang Chao successively held Qi, Xiang Liang rose in the Qi town of Xue, and Xiang Yu, though a Chu man, rode the campaign that destroyed Qin. That grievance at the loss of the state and the memory of its clansmen helped bring the Qin dynasty down quickly.
result: 結果極簡：齊國不戰而降，王朝終結。公元前221年秦王政二十六年，秦軍進臨淄，齊王建遣使降秦，被封為平原君，遷於薛，齊國宗廟與世祀自此斷絕；秦遂以齊地置齊郡、琅邪郡，編戶齊民，收繳其兵器，同年稱皇帝，行皇帝之制，罷分封、行郡縣，書同文，車同軌，度量衡同，統一於此役之後完成，其後東巡刻石、封禪泰山，宣告帝國事業。從軍事結果看，齊人未能在臨淄城下、齊長城線上與秦軍作任何有效抵抗，主力兵員與武庫在交涉中完整地落入秦手，成為秦軍後來北擊匈奴、開疆拓土的補充；從政治結果看，齊國世卿與封國的歷史至此告終，東方大國的封建格局由一場成功的政治兼併收束。史書於此役的記載雖簡，卻留下幾個鮮明的尾巴：秦人收天下兵器聚之咸陽、銷為鐘鐻，漢人賈誼《過秦論》譏其「仁義不施而攻守之勢異也」；而齊王建一支的國脈，則在秦亡之後於楚漢之際由田榮、田儋諸人重新提出，齊地也成為反秦最力之地。
resultEn: The outcome was the simplest possible: Qi surrendered without a battle and the dynasty ended. In 221 BC, in the twenty-sixth year of King Zheng of Qin, the Qin army reached Linzi, King Jian of Qi sent envoys to surrender, was made Lord of Pingyuan and was moved to Xue, and the ancestral temple and the inherited sacrifices of Qi were broken off there for good. Qin then established the commanderies of Qi and Langya over Qi's land, enrolled the people in the registers, gathered in the weapons, and in the same year assumed the title of Huangdi and the institutions of the imperial rule: abolishing enfeoffment, setting up commanderies and counties, one script for all writing, one gauge for the wheels of carts, one standard of measures and weights. The unification was complete after this campaign, and the tours, the carved stones and the sacrifice at Mount Tai that followed announced the imperial enterprise. In military terms, the Qi people were unable to offer any effective resistance either before the walls of Linzi or along the line of the Qi Great Wall, and the main body of their troops and their arsenal passed whole into Qin's hands through the negotiation, becoming a supplement to the Qin armies that would later drive north against the Xiongnu and open new frontiers. In political terms, the history of Qi's hereditary houses and fiefdoms came to an end, and the feudal structure of the great eastern state was wound up by a successful political annexation. The record of this campaign is brief, but it left a few sharp after-effects: Qin gathered the weapons of the realm at Xianyang and melted them into bells and weights, and the Han writer Jia Yi in his Changsha-style essay on the Qin faulted it with the remark that benevolence and righteousness were never put into practice, so that the situations of attack and of defence came to differ. And the state-lineage of King Jian of Qi was raised again in the Chu-Han years after the fall of Qin by men such as Tian Rong and Tian Dan, while the Qi region became the strongest centre of anti-Qin resistance.
